title: Mini & Multiple Roundabouts
whatItIs: Mini-roundabouts follow the same rules as large ones, with less space and less time. At double or multiple roundabouts, treat each one separately.
keyFacts: Give way to traffic from your right, as at any roundabout.

keyFacts.text: You MUST drive round the central marking. Only large vehicles that can't get round may drive over it.

keyFacts: There is less room and less time to signal, so plan your lane and signal early.
Avoid U-turns at mini-roundabouts, and watch out for others making them.
At double and multiple roundabouts, treat each roundabout separately and give way to traffic from the right at each one.

items.title: Mini-roundabout
items.text: Same rules as a big one: give way to traffic from the right.

items.title: The white circle
items.text: Drive round it. Only large vehicles may drive over it if they must.

items.title: U-turns
items.text: Avoid them here, and expect other drivers to make them.

items.title: Double or multiple
items.text: Treat each roundabout on its own. Give way to the right at each one.

a.label: Mini-roundabout sign
points: An order: give way to traffic from the right

b.label: Roundabout ahead sign
points: A warning: a roundabout is coming

onTheTest.question: At a mini-roundabout, which vehicles may drive over the central white circle?
options: Large vehicles that can't get round it
Cars when the roundabout is empty
onTheTest.why: All vehicles must go round the central marking. The only exception is large vehicles that physically can't.

traps: A mini-roundabout is still a roundabout: give way to traffic from the right.
Driving over the white circle in a car breaks the rule.
At a double mini-roundabout, give way at each one, not just the first.
